entityName: TUM - CHAIR OF PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, DESIGN SYSTEMATICS, AND LIGHTWEIGHT DESIGN
entityDescription: The Laboratory for Product Development and Lightweight Design is based at the TUM Department of Mechanical Engineering. Our Laboratory’s research and teaching is about engineering design, i.e., the creation of concrete solutions to specific problems. This is particularly challenging when the solution and its elements are entirely unknown. In so-called top-down approaches, the development focus is on the desired features of the new product rather than on already existing solutions or their elements. Both, methods from product development, such as creativity techniques, and methods from lightweight design, such as physical surrogate modelling, help to explore the unknown and find a way to new solutions to complex problems. For complex problems, it is often important to consider the entire system by adopting a holistic and interdisciplinary view. In both, lightweight design and in product development, all relevant requirements on a product, all aspects of feasibility and constraints on realization, and all interactions of all system components have to be taken into account. How treat the resulting complexity is an important subject of our research and teaching. We cover a large span of different quantitative and qualitative methods ranging, for example, from new numerical optimization techniques from lightweight design to Design Structure Matrices from product development. In order to produce both, applicable and scientifically outstanding results we closely cooperate with many partners from industry and academia.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2014, Faculty Science Ltd (‘Faculty’) is the UK’s largest, independent Applied AI company, with 400 employees, including ~130 PhD+ level qualified data scientists and software engineers, many cleared to SC/DV. We have delivered over 500 AI projects to clients, ranging from small advisory reports to full production-level software used in critical BaU functions. Our services business covers four sectors, (Government, Defence, National Security, Healthcare, Energy Transition, Retail & Consumer) and our product team delivers ‘Frontier’, an AI-enabled supply chain and demand-side forecasting tool for healthcare, commercial and Government clients.
We offer bespoke AI/ML builds, data analytics & visualisation, data strategy, data engineering services and decision intelligence products, helping organisations to understand their data, and take action from subsequent insights. We have links with the AI teams at UCL and Harvard; our own team includes former Front Line users from across all FLCs and domains.
The Defence team formed in Aug 2021, has been the data science partner of Dstl’s ‘Defence AI Centre (Experimentation)’ and the provider of forward-deployed AI/ML expertise and platforms to elements of UKStratCom. We are a member of the RN FASTER programme and are constructing computational digital twins of complex business processes for another FLC, via Dstl. Awaiting List-X accreditation.
We are experienced across a wide range of AI applications, including;
Digital signal processing of acoustic, electric and electromagnetic signals to enable signal detection, conducted for government agencies, Front Line Commands and a UK Defence manufacturer. Includes voice fingerprinting of radio and voice transmission to identify propaganda, or to automate auditing of safety practices involving radio commands.
Intelligence data fusion up to TS, including building ML-specific elements of underlying knowledge platforms, including on MODCloud. Cloud-agnostic development engineering teams have constructed AI platforms for the National Crime Agency, BEIS, Food Standards Agency and elements of UKStratCom. Most experience with AWS, Azure and Palantir Foundry.
Still and moving image object detection, using lightweight models to enable edge-based still image processing Proof of Concept in a harsh-environment Front Line use case. Other examples include an automated trackside maintenance video inspection system for National Rail, an automated nuclear waste sorting and segmentation system for a Civil Nuclear client and a video detector for a sensitive National Crime Agency use case.
NLP tools and platforms for improved intelligence discovery and fast identification of disinformation for UK Government Defence and Security clients, across multiple classifications; often in combination with video and other sources.
Improved route calculation for uncrewed UAVs and USVs, undertaken for multiple clients, combining meteorological, topographical, sensor and vessel performance data.

entityName: AIMPLAS- ASOCIACION DE INVESTIGACION DE MATERIALES PLASTICOS Y CONEXAS
entityDescription: AIMPLAS, Technological Institute of Plastics located in Valencia, is a private, non-profit Association with more than 500 associated companies created in 1990. AIMPLAS is formed by +120 highly skilled professional, more than 65% with a Masters, Engineering or equivalent degree in Chemistry, polymer engineering, materials engineering or equivalent, including 15 PhD. AIMPLAS’ fields of work are related to technological research and development on thermoplastic and thermosetting plastic materials & products, its transformation processes and their recyclability and sustainability. AIMPLAS generates new knowledge and technologies that can be transferred to companies in order to help them to increase their effectiveness and competitiveness. Nowadays, AIMPLAS has participated in 100 EU projects in FP5, FP6, FP7, LIFE+, CIP-EcoInnovation, H2020, among others, coordinating more 30 of them. In H2020, AIMPLAS is participating in more than 18 projects, coordinating most of them. Outstanding LIFE projects were celebrated at the Green Awards ceremony in Brussels on 30 May 2017, BREAD4PLA – with AIMPLAS as a coordinator - was honoured as one of the two most exceptional LIFE projects of the programme's 25-year history. At National and Regional levels AIMPLAS participates in around 100 projects yearly. AIMPLAS, as RO is focused to help companies in the plastic sector to develop new products and increase their competitiveness through innovation, has more than 20 pilot plants representing the most relevant polymer/plastics/composites production technologies present in the industry nowadays and has state-of-the art test facilities for chemical, optical, morphological, mechanical and physical characterisation. These pilot lines and laboratories are used by many customer’s every year allowing them to test new materials, optimize production processes and launch new products to the market, supported by AIMPLAS technical staff, resulting in more than 5000 assays, 170 technical assessments and 120 skills training actions to more than 1500 clients per year. AIMPLAS has state-of-the-art 8500 m2 facilities, including thermoplastics and thermoset pilot plants, analysis and testing laboratories (physical-mechanical, chemical, packaging, automotive and construction) and training areas. Member of any technology platforms, clusters, associations, networks etc. We take part in international and national research networks and technological platforms, with the objective to support the research and competitiveness of enterprises in their use with plastic materials. The interchange of R&D management tools as well as a know-how transfer allow us to be pioneers in the needs of the business field and the latest technologies.

entityName: UNIV FIRENZE - Department of Information Engineering (DINFO)
entityDescription:
Research on informatics, electronics, and telecommunications
The Department of Information Engineering (DINFO), one of the 24 departments of the University of Florence, is the reference Department for ICT (Information and Communications Technology), where it carries out advanced research in control systems, computer science and engineering, electronics systems, electromagnetism, telecommunications, operation research, bioengineering and electrical engineering.
Traditional and advanced researches, designs and implementations are digital signal processing, fixed and wireless telecommunications systems, radar, sensors and electronic devices, advanced software, ultrasound systems, satellite telecommunication/localization/sensing, media content processing and interpretation, decision support , security and protection of information and telematics, ICT for eHealth systems and electrical networks effciency.
DINFO is member of several inter-university centres and consortia, among which CNIT (National Inter-University Consortium for Telecommunications), MECSA (Microwave Engineering Centre for Space Applications), MIDRA (Multidisciplinary Institute for Development Research and Applications) and TICOM (Consortium for Technologies of Information and Telecommunications), which play an important role in the national high-level scientific cooperation between universities and industries.
DINFO also includes MICC (Media Integration and Communication Centre), a centre of excellence established by the Ministry of University and Research in 2001.
DINFO employs a workforce of more than 210 units (including professors, researchers, technical and administrative people, post-doc fellows and PhD students) with success in the acquisition of important public and private research funding. DINFO is in charge of two first-level three-year degree courses (Electronic Engineering and Telecommunications, Computer Engineering), five Master-of-Science two-year courses (Biomedical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical and Automation Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering) and a PhD course in Information Engineering for a total of about 1,400 students.
The main public research funding comes from European Community, the European Space Agency, the Ministry of University and Research, national research programs and the Tuscany Region. More than a quarter of the research budget of the DINFO comes from contracts with private companies that generate a fruitful technological transfer to industry.

entityDescription:
Mathema is a performing research ICT company active since 1987 whose main mission is to support very large public and private organisations in the development of complex information systems, in the analysis and mining of large data sets, in monitoring operations and predict dynamics. In particular the core activities and competencies span from System integration, Very Large database (VLDB) management, Crowd sensed information, Semantic processing, Data Fusion and Mining, Artificial Intelligence/Deep learning, real time Complex Event Processig, Resilience Engeeneirng Big Data predictive analytics, Augmented/Virtual Reality, geodata analysis
Mathema applies its competences in the fields of Government (e.g. Italian Ministry of Foreign Affarins and Intern, Tuscany Region, Civil Protection), Cultural Heritage (e.g. National Central Library of Florence), Business, Safety & Security, Smart City, etc. 
In particular, Mathema manages the entire world wide Italian consulate network and it deals with the electoral election of the Italians living abroad for the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (1.5M of people) . Collaborations with other countries are under negotiation. 
Mathema manages a VLDB of all locations, postal codes and street names in the world, which is more complete and accurate than some well known geographic database such as Google Map. This asset is included as added value in each Mathema solutions when is needed.
Mathema designs and delivers user-driven solutions as Luke Collector, a mobile cloud based application for collecting geographic based multimedia data on the field exploiting technologies such as GPS/EGNOS, 3G,4G/LTE, Wifi, Bluetooth, etc. 
Moreover, Mathema has released Yellow Page Albania for CELESI, one of the most download app in the South Balkan region and sponsored by Vodafone Albania.

Finally, Mathema is collaborating with PIN/Mosis laboratory and Italian Civil Protection for design and developing the next generation of disaster management information system based on system thinking and bayesan network.

Mathema follows the Open Innovation 2.0 approach cooperating with Public administrations, Research institutions and final users, and it is involved in the Tuscany ICT Robotics district with more than 700 enterprises and research institutions. 
Mathema internal organisation is based on the Auftragstaktik model (a.k.a. Mission Command) in order to provide flexibility and goal achievement on time and on budget, i.e. what large organisations ask for a specialised team. To this end great effort is devoted to personnel empowerment.

entityDescription: The primary purpose of the University of Urbino Carlo Bo is the promotion and organization of scientific research and higher education, the processing and transmission of scientific knowledge, the training of all staff, the cultural and professional preparation of students in the permanent and recurrent training, cultural innovation, science and technology in society, and (in forms specific to it) the development of the territory. In order to pursue this primary purpose, the University recognize as fundamental missions teaching, research and public service. The first mission is teaching, that is educating students from undergraduate to the most advanced graduate level. Through our academic programs we transmit knowledge and skills to undergraduate students, stimulate new interpretation and development of knowledge in graduate students, educate individuals for professional careers, provide them with the tools to continue intellectual development over the lifetime. The second mission is doing research by a staff of researchers well introduced in international activities with well provided laboratories, libraries, high-speed telematic networks. Hundreds of disciplines are present in our Departments, in the fields from Biology to Physics, Earth and Environmental Sciences, Social Sciences and Fine Arts, Literature and Foreign Language, Philosophy and Psychology, Mathematics and Informatics. The results of this strong research activities yield a lot of benefit to the University itself and to the industrial and cultural environment. The third mission is generally related to the public service: with an intensive program, agreed with regional stakeholders, the Urbino University disseminates research results and translate scientific discovery and technological application into practical knowledge, especially through industry partnerships, that benefit the Marche region and the Nation.
